page.text:
When the operation of a group is commutative—meaning $x * y = y * x$ for
all pairs of elements—the group is called *abelian* (in honor of Niels
Henrik Abel). In abelian groups, the binary operation is often denoted
additively by $+$, with identity $0$ and inverse $-x$.

Abelian groups are far more algebraically tractable than non-commutative
groups: every subgroup of an abelian group is normal, the set of
homomorphisms between two abelian groups forms an abelian group, and the
Fundamental Theorem of Finitely Generated Abelian Groups provides a
complete, canonical classification into direct sums of cyclic groups.
